body: ## Problem When 'linebreak' pushes a word entirely to the next screen row, the filler cells left on the current row keep whatever highlight was set by the last real character before the break, even when that highlight should not extend past it (e.g. an underline, which looks broken drawn over blank cells). #34392 reports two distinct symptoms in one issue: this underline-bleeding behavior, and concealed text causing incorrect wrap width (a duplicate of the decade-old #14409, fixed separately by #40897). This PR only addresses the former; it does not close #14409. ## Solution Reset decor_attr and area_attr at the filler when their attribute has an underline, undercurl, strikethrough, or overline; otherwise leave them, since a plain background or reverse-video highlight looks correct extending through blank filler cells, regardless of where the pushed-down word happens to end. search_attr keeps the same check, plus its pre-existing on_last_col case (its own match ending exactly here).

comment_data.body: "reverse-video" is a terminal-computing term. It means to swap/inverse foreground and background colors. It's shorthand for the reverse/inverse highlight attribute (`HL_INVERSE`). Do you prefer I change the terminology? I can change it to just "reverse" or something else entirely.

comment_regular_data.body: Proactively applied the same test-reduction principle from #41090's review here too: merged the matchadd()/extmark tests (identical setup, differing only in highlight mechanism) into one, reusing the same buffer/screen and adding an intermediate check to prove the extmark path genuinely redraws (not just coasting on matchadd()'s leftover state).

> This is the underline-bleeding behavior reported in #34392 (duplicate of the decade-old #14409).

does this close #14409 ?

No -- #14409 is entirely about conceal causing incorrect wrap width; this PR fixes an unrelated underline-bleeding bug. #34392 happens to report both symptoms in one issue: the conceal-wrap-width part is the actual #14409 duplicate (fixed by #40897), the underline-bleeding part is what this PR fixes. Updating the description to disambiguate.
